[RFCS.12.3] **The engine's schema registry is the source, not the DSC.**
An encoder must announce every schema the engine holds before the first fact
that uses it ([RFCS.5.1]), or a reader hits [RFCS.5.4] at the first
`FactAssert`. Every such schema came from the loaded artefact ([NFCT.1.1]),
the built-in schemas the program uses with it ([LIMP.12.2]), so the DSC carries
a `SchemaDef` and its `Slot` atoms for each.

An encoder may forward those atoms, extracting them from the DSC bytes by the
DSC framing ([RDSC.2]), or construct them from the schema registry. A
`SchemaDef` it constructs names the schema and may carry an empty
`proto_source`: the `Slot` atoms are the schema's shape on the wire, and a
reader decodes the schema's facts from them, with no artefact ([LFST.8.10]).
